# 1 Enoch Chapter 50 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**50:1** And-in-those-days a-change shall-take-place for-the-holy-and-elect, and-the-light of-days shall-abide-upon-them, and-glory and-honor shall-turn-to-the-holy.

**50:2** On-the-day of-affliction, evil-shall-have-been-stored-up against-the-sinners. And-the-righteous shall-be-victorious in-the-name of-the-Lord of-Spirits; and-He-will-cause-the-others to-witness [this], that-they-may-repent and-forgo-the-works of-their-hands.

**50:3** They-shall-have-no-honor through-the-name of-the-Lord of-Spirits; yet-through-His-name shall-they-be-saved, and-the-Lord of-Spirits will-have-compassion-on-them, for-His-compassion is-great.

**50:4** And-He-is-righteous-also in-His-judgment, and-in-the-presence of-His-glory unrighteousness-also-shall-not-maintain-itself; at-His-judgment-the-unrepentant shall-perish before-Him.

**50:5** "And-from-henceforth I-will-have-no-mercy on-them," says the-Lord of-Spirits.

---

*EMET notes: Ch. 50 introduces a nuance rare in apocalyptic: the possibility of repentance for some sinners (v. 2). The righteous are vindicated, but God causes the wicked to "witness" this in order to prompt repentance. V. 3 is striking: even those who have no honor through God's name may be saved through it if they turn. V. 5 closes the door: after the judgment begins, mercy ceases.*
